c74object.name: mUnit.assert~
c74object.digest: Capture a signal and check it with an expression or against a reference file
c74object.description: mUnit.assert~ is an assert for signals. It records duration ms of its signal inlets into its own buffer~, starting when the suite starts (trigger auto) or on a bang to the left inlet (trigger manual), then evaluates its expression with each channel as a list of samples: in1, and with channels 2 also in2. Everything mUnit.assert does applies to the samples, and the outlet bangs once the capture has been evaluated.
c74object.discussion: The capture starts at the next signal vector. The expression defaults to rms(in1) > 0. The helpers (rms, peak, dc, maxDiff, snr, approx, and freq, the frequency in Hz from the zero crossings) and custom scripts all apply, the scripts receiving the channels as arrays. With reference the capture is compared with a wav file next to the test patch instead. A failed assert keeps its capture as actual.wav in the run's artifacts/ folder. Signal tests need DSP running: the dsp key of the configuration applies a driver, sample rate and vector size for the suite (the NonRealTime driver needs no hardware and makes the suite the same on every machine), starts the tests only once DSP is confirmed running on them, fails the suite if they change while it runs, and restores them afterwards. Give the object a timeout, so a suite with DSP off still ends. Pair it with mUnit.stimulus~ for a repeatable input.

inlet.description: With trigger manual, a bang starts the capture at the next signal vector. Not for test data.

outlet.digest: Bang once the capture has been evaluated

objarg.name: expression
objarg.digest: The JavaScript expression over the captured channels, or a custom assert script
objarg.description: As for mUnit.assert, with in1 and in2 being lists of samples. The default is rms(in1) > 0. Quote an expression that contains commas. Ignored when reference is set.

method.name: bang
method.description: In the left inlet: starts recording duration ms at the next signal vector. With trigger auto the suite start does this for you.

method.name: signal
method.description: In the signal inlets: the channels recorded into the object's own buffer~ and handed to the expression as in1 and in2.

attribute.name: duration
attribute.digest: How much to record, in ms (default 1000)
attribute.description: Converted to samples at the suite's sample rate when the capture starts. The assert evaluates when the last sample is in.

attribute.name: channels
attribute.digest: How many signal inlets to capture: 1 or 2 (default 1)
attribute.description: With 2, the second signal inlet is captured as in2.

attribute.name: trigger
attribute.digest: What starts the capture: auto or manual (default auto)
attribute.description: auto: when the suite starts, at the moment mUnit.loadbang fires. manual: on a bang to the left inlet.

enum.name: manual
enum.digest: On a bang to the left inlet

attribute.name: reference
attribute.digest: A wav file to compare the capture with
attribute.description: The name of a file in references/ next to the test patch (.wav is added if there is no extension). The capture passes when its signal-to-noise ratio against the reference is at least snr dB, aligned within maxLatency samples. A missing reference fails and says how to take it; when taking references (munit run --take-references, takeReferences: true in the configuration, or a takeReferences 1 message to mUnit.handler) the capture is written as a 32-bit float wav. A failure reports the SNR, the largest difference and the latency, and keeps the capture as actual.wav in the run's artifacts/ folder next to a link to the reference. References are compared at the suite's sample rate. When there is no such file in references/, a file of that name on Max's search path is read instead, e.g. @reference jongly.aif compares with the sound Max ships with (at 44.1 kHz); taking references still writes to references/.

attribute.name: snr
attribute.digest: The least signal-to-noise ratio that counts as a match, in dB (default 60)
attribute.description: 60 dB is about 0.1% of the signal. Used with reference.

attribute.name: maxLatency
attribute.digest: How many samples the capture may lead or lag the reference (default 0)
attribute.description: The alignment is found by cross-correlation and reported as latency in the results. 0 compares the signals as they are.

attribute.name: exact
attribute.description: With 1, every sample must match the reference bit for bit, instead of meeting snr.

attribute.name: timeout
attribute.digest: How long the assert may take, in ms (default none)
attribute.description: As for mUnit.assert. Set one, so a suite with DSP off still ends: a capture that never finishes then fails instead of hanging the run until the suite timeout.

attribute.name: name
attribute.digest: A name for the test (default: its UUID)
attribute.description: Used in the console, the log and the results, as for mUnit.assert; suite, maxCalls, skip, only, tolerance and dataInlets apply too.

entry.name: freq(x)
entry.description: The frequency of a captured channel in Hz, from its zero crossings, precise to a fraction of a Hz even for a short capture.

entry.name: rms(x), peak(x), dc(x), maxDiff(a, e), snr(a, reference)
entry.description: Root mean square, largest absolute value, mean, largest difference, and signal-to-noise ratio in dB, over a channel's samples.

entry.name: bang
entry.description: Out the outlet: a bang once the capture has been evaluated and the result reported to mUnit.handler, so a patch can chain the next capture or clean up.
